topic: Market basket analysis: support, confidence and lift
title: Market basket analysis in SQL
instructions:
## Twelve baskets from a Madina supermarket

The **baskets** table has one row per item per basket (basket_id, item). Mine the item pairs.

For a rule A → B (A alphabetically before B): **support** is the number of baskets containing both, **confidence** is support ÷ baskets containing A, and **lift** is confidence ÷ (baskets containing B ÷ all baskets).

## Do this

Return `item_a`, `item_b`, `support`, `confidence` (rounded to 2 dp) and `lift` (rounded to 2 dp) for every pair with support of at least 3 baskets, ordered by lift descending, then item_a, then item_b.

The starter already has the CTEs for total baskets, per-item counts and pair counts. Join them and compute the two ratios.

config.schema:
CREATE TABLE baskets (basket_id INTEGER NOT NULL, item TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (basket_id, item));
INSERT INTO baskets VALUES
  (1,'rice'),(1,'oil'),(1,'tomato paste'),(1,'onion'),
  (2,'rice'),(2,'oil'),(2,'sardines'),
  (3,'bread'),(3,'milk'),(3,'sugar'),
  (4,'rice'),(4,'tomato paste'),(4,'onion'),(4,'oil'),
  (5,'bread'),(5,'milk'),(5,'eggs'),
  (6,'rice'),(6,'oil'),(6,'onion'),
  (7,'bread'),(7,'sugar'),(7,'milk'),(7,'tea'),
  (8,'rice'),(8,'sardines'),(8,'tomato paste'),
  (9,'oil'),(9,'onion'),(9,'tomato paste'),
  (10,'bread'),(10,'eggs'),(10,'milk'),
  (11,'rice'),(11,'oil'),(11,'tomato paste'),
  (12,'sugar'),(12,'tea'),(12,'milk');

initialState.sql:
WITH n AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT basket_id) AS total FROM baskets),
     item_count AS (SELECT item, COUNT(DISTINCT basket_id) AS c FROM baskets GROUP BY item),
     pairs AS (
       SELECT a.item AS item_a, b.item AS item_b, COUNT(*) AS pair_count
       FROM baskets a JOIN baskets b ON a.basket_id = b.basket_id AND a.item < b.item
       GROUP BY a.item, b.item
     )
SELECT item_a, item_b, pair_count AS support
FROM pairs
WHERE pair_count >= 3
ORDER BY support DESC, item_a, item_b;

hints: Join `pairs` to `item_count` twice: once for item_a (ca) and once for item_b (cb); the single-row `n` CTE can be CROSS JOINed.
`ROUND((1.0 * pair_count / ca.c) / (1.0 * cb.c / n.total), 2) AS lift`, then `ORDER BY lift DESC, item_a, item_b`.

checks.label: Support, confidence and lift for every frequent pair
checks.expectedQuery: WITH n AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT basket_id) AS total FROM baskets), item_count AS (SELECT item, COUNT(DISTINCT basket_id) AS c FROM baskets GROUP BY item), pairs AS (SELECT a.item AS item_a, b.item AS item_b, COUNT(*) AS pair_count FROM baskets a JOIN baskets b ON a.basket_id = b.basket_id AND a.item < b.item GROUP BY a.item, b.item) SELECT p.item_a, p.item_b, p.pair_count AS support, ROUND(1.0 * p.pair_count / ca.c, 2) AS confidence, ROUND((1.0 * p.pair_count / ca.c) / (1.0 * cb.c / n.total), 2) AS lift FROM pairs p JOIN item_count ca ON ca.item = p.item_a JOIN item_count cb ON cb.item = p.item_b CROSS JOIN n WHERE p.pair_count >= 3 ORDER BY lift DESC, p.item_a, p.item_b

checks.label: It computes lift
checks.message: Name the lift column lift: confidence divided by the base rate of item_b.

realityNote: Apriori and FP-growth exist because this self-join explodes on millions of baskets and thousands of items; on a small table, plain SQL gives the same rules.
